Implementation-relevant•Peer-reviewed retrospective imaging cohort•September 17, 2026

Cerebellar amyloid can bias florbetapir Centiloid quantification

In 359 amyloid-positive participants, cerebellar cortical amyloid raised the whole-cerebellum reference signal and could systematically underestimate cortical florbetapir burden; a white-matter-normalized cerebellar threshold showed strong internal discrimination but needs external validation.

Key quantitative results: Participants with cerebellar cortical amyloid had higher whole-cerebellum reference SUV (p=0.012) but lower cortical SUV (p=0.008), producing lower whole-cerebellum-referenced Centiloid estimates despite cortical amyloid burden; pons SUV did not differ significantly (p=0.110).

BiomarkersAmyloid PETAmyloidPET quantification

Added September 18, 2026 · DOI:10.1007/s00259-026-08140-6; PMID:42749937

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

Whole cerebellum is commonly treated as a stable reference region for amyloid PET, but this study shows that cerebellar amyloid can inflate the denominator and depress cortical SUVR and Centiloid values. The proposed screen may help identify affected scans, but it was derived and validated internally and is not a clinical cutoff.

Study design

Retrospective analysis of 359 amyloid-positive participants who had 18F-florbetapir PET, MRI and CSF biomarkers; 52 had visually defined cerebellar cortical amyloid deposition and 307 did not. A white-matter-normalized cerebellar SUVR threshold was derived and internally validated in 30 additional cases.

Key quantitative results

  • Participants with cerebellar cortical amyloid had higher whole-cerebellum reference SUV (p=0.012) but lower cortical SUV (p=0.008), producing lower whole-cerebellum-referenced Centiloid estimates despite cortical amyloid burden; pons SUV did not differ significantly (p=0.110).
  • A white-matter-normalized cerebellar SUVR threshold of 0.428 distinguished cerebellar deposition with AUC 0.931, 86.5% sensitivity and 86.3% specificity; internal validation in 30 cases yielded kappa 0.856.
  • In two lecanemab-treated cases, cortical Centiloid values declined longitudinally while cerebellar white-matter-normalized SUVR remained above the proposed threshold.

What changed

A dedicated analysis quantified a clinically relevant reference-region failure mode and proposed an internal screen for cerebellar amyloid before interpreting whole-cerebellum-referenced florbetapir measurements.

Strength of evidence

Moderate measurement-validity evidence: the cohort was sizeable and included internal validation, but all participants were already amyloid positive, only 52 had cerebellar deposition, validation included 30 cases and longitudinal treatment observations were limited to two people.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

When serial or borderline florbetapir measurements appear discordant with the cortical image pattern, cerebellar reference contamination should be considered before inferring low burden or treatment response. The proposed threshold is not ready for routine clinical decisions without external validation.

Field medical relevance

Useful for interpreting Centiloid values, selecting reference regions in trials and explaining why reference-region biology can alter quantitative amyloid PET results even when the tracer and cortical signal are unchanged.

Quanterix or platform relevance

The finding concerns reference-region selection and quantification of 18F-florbetapir PET. The 0.428 white-matter-normalized threshold should not be transferred to other tracers, scanners or processing pipelines without validation.

Access or reimbursement relevance

No authorization, commercial availability, formal guideline endorsement, coverage or reimbursement change follows from this study.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Does this establish a new clinical cutoff?
No. The 0.428 threshold was derived and validated within the same research program and requires external, scanner- and pipeline-specific validation.
Should whole cerebellum no longer be used as a reference region?
Not categorically. The study identifies a subgroup in whom whole-cerebellum normalization may be biased; it does not compare all reference strategies prospectively or establish a universal replacement.
Does the study prove better clinical outcomes with another reference region?
No. It addresses measurement interpretation, not clinical utility or patient outcomes.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • Retrospective, single-program analysis restricted to amyloid-positive participants
  • Only 52 participants had cerebellar cortical deposition
  • The proposed threshold had internal rather than independent external validation
  • Only two anti-amyloid-treated cases contributed longitudinal treatment examples
  • No prospective decision-impact or patient-outcome assessment

Primary source · DOI · PubMed record
